summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale in complexity and cost, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on token consumption, latency regressions, prompt drift, and failure modes that silently degrade user experience. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, underscoring how rapidly it has shifted from nice-to-have to essential infrastructure.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM chains, agents, prompts, retrieval steps, and evaluation runs — primarily within LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems but also framework-agnostic via SDK
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Dataset management and regression testing
Prompt versioning and A/B comparison
Human annotation and feedback collection
Online evaluations with custom scorers
LangChain-native deep integration
Latency and token usage breakdowns per run
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overages around $2.50 per 1,000 traces; Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £80/month for 100K traces at standard usage.
tools.best_for: Teams heavily invested in the LangChain or LangGraph ecosystem who need the richest debugging, evaluation, and prompt management workflow tightly coupled to their orchestration framework.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses as a proxy gateway, covering cost per request, token usage, latency, error rates, and model comparisons across providers
features: One-line proxy setup (2-minute integration)
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and user-level usage controls
Multi-provider support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Gemini, etc.)
Custom properties and metadata tagging
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (adds SOC-2 and HIPAA); Enterprise custom. Approximately £20/month for 100K traces — the most cost-effective managed option.
tools.best_for: Cost-sensitive teams that want the fastest setup and best-in-class spend visibility across multiple LLM providers without complex instrumentation.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM experiments, prompt iterations, evaluation metrics, training runs, and production traces — bridging the gap between model development and deployment monitoring
features: Experiment tracking tightly integrated with LLM fine-tuning workflows
Weave tracing for production LLM calls and agents
Evaluation pipelines with custom scoring functions
Dataset versioning and artifact management
Collaborative dashboards for team review
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM libraries
Side-by-side prompt and output comparisons
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/user/month; Enterprise custom pricing. Consumption-based overages apply for storage and compute beyond included limits.
tools.best_for: ML-native teams who are simultaneously fine-tuning models and deploying LLM applications and need a single platform spanning research experimentation through production observability.

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM spans, traces, embeddings, retrieval quality, agent workflows, and broader ML model performance — extending traditional ML monitoring into generative AI workloads
features: Span-level tracing for complex multi-step LLM pipelines
Experiment-style workflows for prompt and model comparison
Embedding drift and clustering visualization
RAG retrieval quality evaluation (context precision, recall)
OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation
Online and offline evaluation support
Enterprise-grade telemetry at scale
Open-source Phoenix library for local and self-hosted use
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host. Arize AI managed platform offers a free tier; paid plans are enterprise-negotiated and consumption-based, typically suited for larger organizations. Details require direct contact for enterprise quotes.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams that need deep telemetry across both traditional ML models and LLM workloads, particularly those running RAG pipelines or complex agent architectures requiring span-level trace analysis.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost, latency, and custom evaluation scores across any LLM provider or framework
features: OpenTelemetry-native tracing and instrumentation
Prompt management with versioning and rollback
Custom score hooks for human and automated evaluation
Session and user-level analytics
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and REST API
Self-hostable with full data sovereignty
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI SDK, and more
Free Cloud tier for up to 50K requests/month
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid Cloud plans from approximately £20/month for higher volumes (up to 500K requests); Self-hosted free (open-source MIT license) with roughly £30/month infrastructure cost and ~2 hours/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams that want full tracing, prompt management, and evaluation in a self-hostable package with strong OpenTelemetry compatibility and no vendor lock-in.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and errors across any provider by instrumenting existing code with OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry — acts as an instrumentation layer rather than a standalone platform
features: OpenTelemetry-based SDK for automatic LLM instrumentation
Provider-agnostic (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, HuggingFace, etc.)
Drop-in compatibility with any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, Langfuse, etc.)
Trace context propagation across microservices
Minimal code changes required for adoption
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
Supports Python and JavaScript/TypeScript
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Costs depend only on the observability backend you export data to (e.g., Grafana Cloud, Datadog, or self-hosted Jaeger/OpenObserve).
tools.best_for: Teams that already have an OpenTelemetry-compatible observability stack and want to add LLM-specific instrumentation without adopting a new vendor platform, maintaining backend flexibility.

tools.name: OpenObserve
tools.monitors: Unified observability across LLM traces, application logs, infrastructure metrics, and frontend (RUM) monitoring — eliminating the need for a separate LLM observability tool alongside a DevOps stack
features: Unified LLM tracing alongside logs, metrics, and RUM in one platform
Prompt tracing and cost tracking
Online evaluations for production LLM outputs
OpenTelemetry-native ingestion
Significantly lower storage costs than Elasticsearch alternatives
Self-hostable and cloud-managed options
SQL-based query interface for flexible analysis
Dashboards for infrastructure and AI workloads side by side
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted version is free. Cloud managed plan starts with a free tier; paid tiers are consumption-based on data ingested. Self-hosting on modest infrastructure can run under $50/month for many mid-size teams.
tools.best_for: Platform and DevOps teams who want to consolidate their entire observability stack — LLM tracing, application logs, and infrastructure metrics — into a single deployment rather than managing multiple specialized tools.

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality through evaluation metrics including correctness, hallucination, toxicity, RAG faithfulness, contextual relevance, and 50+ additional open-sourced metrics via DeepEval
features: 50+ evaluation metrics open-sourced through DeepEval
Evaluation integrated directly into the observability layer
Regression testing for prompt and model changes
RAG pipeline evaluation (faithfulness, context precision, recall)
CI/CD integration for automated quality gates
Used by teams at OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft
Dataset management for evaluation benchmarking
Real-time and batch evaluation modes
tools.pricing: DeepEval core library is open-source and free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier for individuals; Team and Enterprise plans are available with pricing on request based on evaluation volume and seats.
tools.best_for: Evaluation-first teams who prioritize output quality assurance, hallucination detection, and RAG pipeline accuracy over infrastructure monitoring, and want the most comprehensive evaluation metric library available.

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: Tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical requests return stored responses without hitting the LLM API, which can reduce costs by 20-40% for applications with repetitive queries such as FAQ bots or templated workflows.

Right-size your model selection per task: Use cheaper, faster models (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku, or Gemini Flash) for simple classification, routing, or extraction tasks, and reserve expensive frontier models only for complex reasoning steps — observability tools with per-trace cost breakdowns make it easy to identify which pipeline steps are driving the most spend.

Set token budgets and enforce output length limits: A large share of LLM costs come from verbose outputs. Instrument your prompts with explicit max_token constraints and monitor average output token counts in your observability dashboard; even reducing average response length by 20% compounds into significant savings at scale.

Monitor and eliminate zombie usage with user-level and session-level analytics: Observability platforms like Langfuse, Helicone, and LangSmith let you break down costs by user, session, or feature — enabling you to identify runaway agents, infinite retry loops, or low-value features consuming disproportionate API budget, so you can throttle or redesign them before costs escalate.
